b.answer:
Worked example: a fictional hair salon in Enugu. The owner, Adaeze, was interviewed for 30 minutes about last week.

DISCOVERY NOTES · Adaeze's Salon, Enugu · [date]
Business: braids, wigs, nails; 4 stylists; WhatsApp and walk-ins; busiest Fri–Sat
Why now: "Two Saturdays ago three clients didn't show and I turned people away."
Week walk-through: every evening spent confirming bookings on WhatsApp
Chosen process: booking request on WhatsApp → check paper diary → reply with a
  slot → write it in → reminder the night before (when she remembers)
Numbers, her words: "about an hour every evening on bookings" ·
  "two or three no-shows a week" · "a missed braiding slot is ₦8,000 gone"
Data: paper diary; names and phone numbers; no health data
Success in 3 months: "No empty chairs on Saturday that I didn't know about."
Constraints: WhatsApp stays; budget "not more than ₦300,000"; Adaeze decides
Red flags: none; diary sometimes incomplete
Next step agreed: she checks the map; I send a scope
  • Before: request arrives (manual) → check diary (manual) → reply with a slot (manual) → reminder the night before, often forgotten (manual).
  • After: request logged to a Bookings sheet (automated) → Adaeze picks the slot (human decision) → confirmation sent (automated) → reminder the day before, YES/NO reply logged (automated) → a NO frees the slot for Adaeze to refill (human decision).

Owner check: map read back to Adaeze at minute 28. She corrected step 2: her sister also takes bookings. Map updated and agreed.
mistakes: Asking how things "usually" work, so the notes describe the ideal process instead of last week's real one.
Writing your own estimates instead of the owner's numbers in their own words, with no quote marks or source.
Drawing only the "after" map, or not labelling steps as manual, automated or human decision.
Assuming the owner agrees with the map instead of reading it back and recording their correction.
b.pass: Notes follow the discovery template and quote at least three numbers in the owner's words (time, frequency, cost); the before-and-after map labels every step, and there's a note of when the owner checked and agreed it.
b.redo: Send it back if the numbers are the learner's guesses, the map shows only the new process, or there's no sign the owner saw and agreed the map.

s.answer:
Worked example: the scope for the fictional Enugu salon from Bronze.

SCOPE · Adaeze's Salon: Booking Reminders · v1 · [date]
1. Background: "about an hour every evening on bookings"; "two or three
   no-shows a week", each "₦8,000 gone".
2. Goal: no-shows at 1 a week or fewer; booking admin under 2 h/week.
3. In scope:
   a. Daily 18:00: tomorrow's bookings (shared sheet) → WhatsApp utility
      template: "Hello {{name}}, your appointment at Adaeze's Salon is
      tomorrow at {{time}}. Reply YES to confirm or NO to cancel."
   b. Replies logged; NO marks the slot free and alerts Adaeze.
   c. Monday summary: bookings, confirmations, no-shows.
4. Out of scope: deposits or online payment; a booking chatbot; Instagram
   and Facebook messages; staff rota and commissions; marketing broadcasts;
   any app; more than 2 staff accounts.
5. Client provides: verified WhatsApp business number (start in week 1);
   client list with consent to reminders; bookings typed in daily; 2 h for tests.
6. Deliverables: workflows, one-page guide, 30-minute training, demo video.
7. Timeline: wk 1 map sign-off · wk 2 build · wk 3 test · wk 4 go-live.
8. Price: setup ₦250,000 (50% to start, 50% at go-live); ₦15,000/month for
   hosting, messages up to an agreed volume, monitoring and fixes.
9. Acceptance: 20 test bookings get the right reminder at the right time;
   10 test NO replies free the slot and alert Adaeze; nobody without
   recorded consent is messaged.
10. Risks: Meta verification delays; bookings not typed in.
11. Changes: quoted separately as change requests.
Value lineWorkingSource
Time6 h/week × 52 ÷ 12 × ₦1,200 × 70% = ₦21,840"an hour every evening", 6 days; assistant's hourly pay
No-shows10 a month × ₦8,000 × 70% = ₦56,000"two or three a week"; "₦8,000 gone"
Refilled slots₦20,000 a monthAssumption agreed with Adaeze: 2–3 freed slots rebooked
TotalValue ₦97,840; net after ₦15,000 = ₦82,840Payback ₦250,000 ÷ ₦82,840 ≈ 3.0 months
mistakes: Fewer than five out-of-scope items, or vague ones like "other features".
Acceptance criteria that can't be run, such as "reminders work well".
Payback that counts 100% of the task, or has numbers with no source.
Leaving out what the client provides, especially WhatsApp verification and consent.
s.pass: Every template section is filled, with at least five specific out-of-scope items, acceptance tests with counts, a dated timeline, setup and monthly price with payment terms, and a payback table where every figure has a source. A friend who wasn't on the call can say what is and isn't delivered.
s.redo: Send it back if out of scope or client responsibilities are missing, acceptance tests are vague, or the payback has unsourced numbers or runs past six months without comment.

g.answer:
Worked example: a learner's discovery kit, tested with a fictional submission from Bright Future School, Abeokuta.

  1. Questionnaire (n8n Form): business, contact name, email, WhatsApp number, what you sell, staff, busiest days, "the task that eats most of your week", hours a week on it, tools used, budget range, and a consent tick ("You may store these answers to prepare our call"). No health, card or ID details.
  2. Call script: the four blocks from Card 1.
  3. Map template: an Excalidraw file with Before and After rows and the manual / automated / human decision legend.
  4. Payback sheet: the Card 3 inputs plus a Source column.
  5. Scope template: Card 4 as a Google Doc.
DK · Discovery intake (n8n, published)
1. n8n Form Trigger: the questionnaire
2. Edit Fields: ref = DK-{{ $now.toFormat('MMdd') }}-{{ $json.business.slice(0,3).toUpperCase() }}
3. Google Drive · Copy file: "Discovery notes TEMPLATE" → "{{ref}} · {{business}}"
4. Google Docs · Update (replace text): [[business]] [[task]] [[hours]]
   [[tools]] [[budget]] → the form answers
5. Gmail · Send to the client: thanks, your booking link (Calendly or
   similar), the ref
6. Gmail · Send to you: pre-call summary + link to the new notes doc
7. Settings: error workflow (3.6) connected

Evidence from one test submission:

Subject: Pre-call · DK-0603-BRI · Bright Future School, Abeokuta
Task: fee reminders to parents, "about 8 hours a week"
Tools: WhatsApp, Excel · Budget: ₦200,000–₦400,000
Flags: children's and parents' data; consent wording needed
Notes doc: [link] (all 5 placeholders filled) · Booking link sent: yes

Submit: the form link, a cleaned export of the workflow, the execution log of the test run, screenshots of the filled doc and both emails, and the five kit files. Use fictional test answers only.
mistakes: Asking for sensitive data the call doesn't need (health, card or ID numbers), with no consent line.
Writing into the master template instead of copying it first, so the next submission overwrites the last.
Using {{ }} placeholders in the doc, which clash with n8n expressions; use a distinct marker such as [[business]].
Testing with pinned data and "Execute step" instead of a real submission to the published form.
g.pass: One real submission to the published form creates a new, correctly named notes doc with every placeholder filled, sends the booking-link email and the pre-call summary, and the execution log shows no manual step. All five kit pieces are attached.
g.redo: Send it back if placeholders are left unfilled, the template itself was overwritten, any step was run by hand, or kit pieces are missing.
